conceptual assets.concept: External-reset deassertion state and output (extended external reset)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The sequencer implements an external-reset extension and drives the external reset output: when rstn_ext_i = '0' the code sets sreg_ext <= (others => '0') and rstn_ext_o <= '0'; on rising_edge(clk_i) sreg_ext <= sreg_ext(sreg_ext'left-1 downto 0) & '1' and rstn_ext_o <= and_reduce_f(sreg_ext). The module's behavior depends on sreg_ext to decide rstn_ext_o; corruption of sreg_ext or rstn_ext_o would violate that implemented deassertion/extension relation, establishing an Integrity objective. Structural realization: the shift register stores the state and rstn_ext_o is the exit for the decision.

conceptual assets.concept: System-reset deassertion state and output (system reset gating and extension)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The sequencer produces rstn_sys_o from an internal shift register and forces it when other resets assert: on rstn_ext_i = '0' the code sets sreg_sys <= (others => '0') and rstn_sys_o <= '0'; on rising_edge(clk_i) if (rstn_wdt_i = '0') or (rstn_dbg_i = '0') then sreg_sys <= (others => '0') else sreg_sys <= sreg_sys(sreg_sys'left-1 downto 0) & '1'; rstn_sys_o <= and_reduce_f(sreg_sys). The implemented relation between sreg_sys and rstn_sys_o is the module's system-reset decision; corruption of that state or the output breaks the implemented reset gating (Integrity).

conceptual assets.concept: Synchronized watchdog and debug reset outputs
conceptual assets.reasoning: The synchronizer samples the asynchronous watchdog and debug reset inputs into synchronous outputs: when rstn_ext_i = '0' the process sets xrstn_wdt_o <= '0' and xrstn_ocd_o <= '0'; otherwise on rising_edge(clk_i) it assigns xrstn_wdt_o <= rstn_wdt_i and xrstn_ocd_o <= rstn_dbg_i. The RTL therefore defines these synchronized outputs as the sampled reset values; incorrect xrstn_wdt_o or xrstn_ocd_o would violate that sampling relation (Integrity).

The clock module generates one-cycle enable pulses on selected counter-bit rising edges: e.g. clk_en_o(clk_div2_c) <= cnt(0) and (not cnt2(0)); ... clk_en_o(clk_div4096_c) <= cnt(11) and (not cnt2(11)). These assignments implement the pulse-generation relation from the counter state; an incorrect clk_en_o value would violate the implemented timing/pulse relation (Integrity).

The ticker process computes and stores an overall enable that gates counting: en <= or_reduce_f(enable_i) (at clock) and the code uses if (en = '1') then cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1) else cnt <= (others => '0');. en therefore controls whether counters advance and pulses are generated; corruption of en would break that gating behavior (Integrity).

conceptual assets.concept: Clock-division counter state used to time enable pulses (cnt, cnt2)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The ticker stores the counter and its previous value to detect bit transitions: cnt is incremented when enabled via cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1); cnt2 <= cnt captures the prior value. Pulse generation uses cnt(bit) and (not cnt2(bit)). The correctness of cnt/cnt2 determines pulse timing; corruption of these registers would violate the implemented timing relations (Integrity).
